record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: How can secure aggregation be made simultaneously efficient, robust, and privacy-preserving when the server may be stronger than semi-honest, when per-round aggregates may leak information, when sparse vectors must be aggregated efficiently, and when client inputs must be checked for well-formedness?

evidence.quote: However, this approach has several limitations: (a) it assumes a semi-honest server (only in the private key infrastructure phase), (b) it allows the server to see the per-round aggregates (which may still leak information), (c) it is not efﬁcient for sparse vector aggregation, and (d) it lacks the ability to enforce well-formedness of client inputs. It is an open question how to construct an efﬁcient and robust secure aggregation protocol that addresses all of these challenges.

artifact.status_search_result: Secure aggregation remains an active research area. While numerous works since 2019 have addressed individual subsets of the listed limitations (malicious-server security, integration with differential privacy, sparse/compressed aggregation, and input validation via zero-knowledge proofs such as Prio/Prio+, RoFL, ACORN, Flamingo, and others), no single protocol is widely recognized as efficiently and robustly solving all four challenges simultaneously at federated-learning scale. The combined problem is therefore generally regarded as still open.

status_evidence.title: ACORN: Input Validation for Secure Aggregation
status_evidence.snippet: ACORN extends secure aggregation with input validation but does not simultaneously address malicious-server setup and aggregate leakage.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works tackle input validation but not all four limitations together.

status_evidence.title: Flamingo: Multi-Round Single-Server Secure Aggregation
status_evidence.snippet: Flamingo improves multi-round secure aggregation efficiency and dropout robustness; orthogonal protocols address sparsity and validation separately.
status_evidence.claim: Progress on robustness and efficiency, but combined goals remain unmet in one protocol.

3. Achieves communication and computation cost that scales with the effective sparsity of the inputs rather than the ambient dimension $d$;
4. Allows the server (or the protocol participants collectively) to efficiently verify well-formedness of each client's input $x_i^{(t)}$ with respect to a prescribed predicate;
5. Remains efficient and robust to client dropouts at federated-learning scale (large $n$, large $d$).
